message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Here’s an overview of key rights you typically enjoy: | Category | Typical Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition; repair structural defects, plumbing, heating, etc. | If landlord fails to fix major issues, tenants may withhold rent or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” claim. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (usually 24 hours) except in emergencies. | Notice must specify time and purpose. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | Landlords may not refuse to rent or impose different terms because of protected characteristics. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for residential rentals > 1 year.
• Lease must disclose: rent amount, security deposit, pet policy, utilities, late fees, etc. | Oral agreements are enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must comply with lease terms and give proper notice (usually 30 days). | For some cities, local ordinances may impose limits. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Court process required; unlawful detainer suit. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent, provided they follow procedure (notice, receipts). | Must keep records and notify landlord. | | **Right to Access Records** | • Tenant can inspect lease, maintenance logs, and other documents. | Landlord must provide reasonable access. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential services (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | Lease may assign responsibility for certain utilities. | ### Practical Steps If You Encounter Issues 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, photos of problems, written communication with landlord. 2. **Serve Written Notice** – Provide written notice of problem and request repair; keep a copy and proof of delivery (certified mail, email read receipt). 3. **Check Local Ordinances** – Some Texas cities (e.g., Austin, Houston) have additional tenant protections (rent control, eviction moratoria). 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If landlord refuses to comply, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. Many communities offer free or low‑cost legal assistance. --- #### Quick Reference: How to Serve a Notice | Notice Type | Purpose | Required Timeframe | Sample Language | |-------------|---------|--------------------|-----------------| | **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** | Nonpayment of rent | 3 days (or 30 days for lease termination) | “You are hereby notified that you owe $X in unpaid rent. Pay within 3 days or vacate.” | | **Notice to Cure or Quit** | Violation of lease (e.g., unauthorized pets) | 30 days | “You are hereby notified that you are violating the lease by having a pet. Correct within 30 days or vacate.” | | **Notice of Entry** | Landlord entry | 24 hours prior | “Landlord will enter on [date] at [time] to perform repairs.” | --- If you’re dealing with a specific situation—like a landlord refusing to make repairs, or you believe you’ve been discriminated against—feel free to describe it, and I can help draft a formal letter or outline next steps.
